question_template: I'm assembling a speech set and right now I only need {wanted} speakers. Based on this clip, should I accept or reject it?
My inclusion rule for this batch is {wanted} speakers only. Does this recording pass? Answer accept or reject.
If the filter keeps {wanted} speakers and drops everything else, what happens to this clip? Explain briefly.
answer_template: {'It is kept, because the speaker here is ' + gender + ', which is what the filter keeps.' if gender == wanted else 'It is dropped, because the speaker here is ' + gender + ' and the filter keeps only ' + wanted + ' speakers.'}

question_template: My set still needs {wanted} speakers. Does this clip match what I'm after, or should I keep looking?
answer_template: {'It matches.' if gender == wanted else 'Keep looking.'}

question_template: I already have plenty of {wanted} speakers and want to skip any more of them. Keep this clip or skip it?
answer_template: {'Skip it.' if gender == wanted else 'Keep it.'}

question_template: Listen to this recording. If my current quota is {wanted} speakers only, accept or reject?
Two folders: one for {wanted} speakers, one for everything else. Which does this clip go in? Explain briefly.
answer_template: {'The ' + wanted + ' folder, since that is how this speaker is labelled.' if gender == wanted else 'The other folder, since this speaker is ' + gender + ' rather than ' + wanted + '.'}

question_template: I need {wanted} voices for this batch. Does this clip qualify? Answer yes or no.
What size vocal folds would you typically expect from a speaker like the one in this clip, and why does that matter for pitch? Explain briefly.
Would you typically expect a longer or a shorter vocal tract from a speaker like the one in this clip?
How does the vocal tract length you would typically expect for this clip's speaker affect their formant spacing? Explain briefly.
If you were picking a vocal tract length normalisation warp for the speaker in this clip, would you warp toward a longer or a shorter tract?
Listen to this clip. Are the formants of a voice like this one typically packed closer together or spread further apart? Answer cautiously.
This corpus files every speaker under either male or female. Which of the two does this clip not carry?
If you had to rule out one of the two gender labels for the speaker in this clip, which would you rule out?
Of the two gender labels in this scheme, name the one this clip's speaker is not.
Listen to this recording. Of male and female, which label does the speaker not fall under?
If a recogniser were trained only on recordings like this clip, what kinds of voices would it most likely serve worse? Answer cautiously.
A team has collected only voices like the one in this clip. In terms of speaker gender, what should they add for balance?
answer_template: {sem(gender, 'other_label').capitalize()}-labelled speakers, to cover the other category in the two-way scheme.

question_template: Name the kind of voice a training set built solely from recordings like this clip would lack.
If you were checking a corpus for speaker gender coverage and every clip looked like this one, what would you flag? Explain briefly.
answer_template: That the corpus carries only {gender} speakers, because {because(gender, 'coverage_gap')}, though {caveat(gender, 'coverage_gap')}.

question_template: Listen to this recording. If it were the only kind of voice in a training set, which voices would go under-served?
A colleague says their model works for everyone, but they only ever tested it on voices like the one in this clip. What would you push back on? Explain briefly.
answer_template: That the test set leaves out {sem(gender, 'other_label')}-labelled speakers entirely, because {because(gender, 'coverage_gap')}, though {caveat(gender, 'coverage_gap')}.

Using the convention 1 for male and 0 for female, what is this clip's speaker gender code?
Give the speaker's gender on this recording as a two-element one-hot vector ordered [male, female].
Under the speaker gender coding scheme (A) male, (B) female, which letter applies to this recording?
Listen to the clip. Under the speaker gender scheme (A) female, (B) male, which letter applies?
Map this clip's speaker gender to a boolean is_female flag. Answer true or false.
Voices like the one in this clip typically sit in which pitch range, roughly 85-155 Hz or roughly 165-255 Hz? Answer cautiously.
Of the two typical adult pitch ranges, 85-155 Hz and 165-255 Hz, which one do voices like the one in this clip usually fall in?
On average, do speakers with this clip's gender label speak at a lower or a higher pitch than the other group?
Do voices like the one in this clip usually have the higher average speaking pitch of the two groups? Answer yes or no.
If you were setting the search range on a pitch tracker for the speaker in this clip, would you centre it lower or higher? Explain briefly.
Listen to this clip. Which pitch range do voices like this usually fall in, 85-155 Hz or 165-255 Hz? Answer cautiously.
If you played this clip alongside a voice from the other gender group, which of the two would usually sound lower in pitch? Explain briefly.
answer_template: {'This one' if sem(gender, 'f0_direction') == 'lower' else 'The other one'}, because {because(gender, 'f0_direction')}, though {caveat(gender, 'f0_direction')}.
